title: Make PosedSkeleton finite-by-construction and define the rig host-space contract
description:
## Summary

Make runtime pose injection finite-by-construction and make the rig's creature-space vs world-space host-transform contract explicit. An external audit (P1) found `PosedSkeleton.WithUpdatedPositions` accepts arbitrary `Vector3` including NaN/Infinity, which can reach `CreatureRig.ApplyPose` and pollute transforms/derived rotations.

Provenance: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-deep-dive-code-review-2026-09-05.md` P1 (PosedSkeleton finite) and P2 (CreatureRig creature-space vs world-space ambiguity). Verified at current HEAD `99fe6ad`. Broad owner family: TSK-0073 (pose/rig) / TSK-0118 (indexed pose-application residuals); no existing TSK owns this finite-pose validation explicitly.

## Scope

- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Animation/Ik/PosedSkeleton.cs`: `WithUpdatedPositions` must reject any non-finite update value using the existing shared `NumericValidity.IsFinite(Vector3)`. Reject earlier (at the pose-mutation boundary) so downstream pose application does not need to defensively sanitize arbitrary vectors.
- State the invariant "PosedSkeleton is finite-by-construction" in the type docs.
- Document the `CreatureRig` space contract: either (a) `CreatureRig` is a world-space adapter that transforms creature-space pose coordinates by the rig root transform, or (b) `CreatureRig` must live at identity as an explicit invariant. Pick one, update the class comment, and cover it with a focused test.
- Do not change pose math or locomotion ownership (locomotion stays out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `WithUpdatedPositions` throws `DomainException` for a NaN or Infinity in each vector component; a fully finite update is accepted.
- The chosen `CreatureRig` space contract is documented and covered by a focused test (identity-root reference behavior and/or non-identity root behavior per the chosen contract).
- No regression in existing IK / pose-application behavior.

## Validation

Focused runtime/EditMode tests for finite pose rejection and the rig root-space contract. Run the full Unity runtime suites. Static source inspection alone cannot close this task.

## Findings

- `WithUpdatedPositions` only checks that the bone ID exists, then writes the supplied vector directly into the new pose with no finite validation.
- The wider runtime already treats finite authored state as a hard precondition (`TransformData.IsFinite` -> `NumericValidity`).
- `BoneSnapshot.Position`/`BonePose` describe creature-space frames while `CreatureRig` assigns them to `Transform.position`; the host-transform (identity) assumption is implicit.

## Blockers

None known.

## Next Step

Add the finite guard and decide/document the rig space contract, then add the focused tests.

comments.body:
Round 2 implementation complete.

Hypothesis (stated before editing): WithUpdatedPositions accepted NaN/Infinity and wrote it into the pose; CreatureRig host-space contract undocumented. Discriminating check: finite guard makes previously-accepted NaN update throw DomainException; rig contract documented + tested. Both confirmed.

Changes:
- PosedSkeleton.cs: private constructor (single creation choke point) now rejects non-finite positions -> finite-by-construction for ALL creation paths (FromRestPose + WithUpdatedPositions). WithUpdatedPositions rejects non-finite per-update at the pose-mutation boundary with a bone-identifying DomainException. Uses existing shared NumericValidity.IsFinite(Vector3) (no second guard). Type docs state "PosedSkeleton is finite-by-construction".
- CreatureRig.cs: class comment now states the space contract explicitly (option b): CreatureRig applies creature-space coordinates directly as world transforms and is NOT a world-space adapter composing the host transform, so the host GameObject must remain at identity (explicit invariant). Chose (b) over (a) because (a) would require composing host transform = pose-math/ApplyPose semantic change, out of scope.
- New PosedSkeletonTests.cs: NaN-per-component, Infinity-per-component, fully-finite accepted, non-finite rest pose rejected.
- CreatureRigTests.cs: two host-space contract tests (identity-root reference; non-identity root does not offset bones -> why host must stay identity).

Validation evidence:
- dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore: succeeded, exit 0, 0 errors/0 warnings.
- dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore: succeeded, exit 0, 0 errors/0 warnings.
- git diff --check: clean (exit 0).
- Unity EditMode (connected editor): full editor suite 125/125 passed.
- Unity PlayMode runtime suite: 507/507 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. New tests confirmed passing: PosedSkeletonTests (4) + CreatureRigTests RigHostSpace (2).

Residual risk: chose documentation + focused test for the rig identity invariant rather than a runtime guard/throw, to avoid changing ApplyPose/Build semantics (out of scope). No pose math or locomotion touched.
